projects.name: Shoot the Moon
projects.summary: A 3D lunar strategy game built for phone browsers. Land, mine, build, strike, survive the counterattack and defend your claim on the Moon.
projects.whatItProves: Ambitious 3D browser work can be built with real test coverage behind it.
projects.hardPart: Keeping player saves compatible while the game kept growing. The save schema is at v9, with migration support for saves from v1 through v8.
projects.howItWasBuilt: React 19, TypeScript, Three.js and React Three Fiber on Vite. The game uses zero external 3D model files and two NASA lunar textures. Verification: 576 unit tests across 63 files and 24 Playwright spec files.

proofSignals: Save schema v9 with v1 to v8 migrations

projects.name: PermitPulse
projects.subtitle: Public-record software evolved into a human-reviewed California property research service.
projects.currentStatus: Three California properties for $299 total. Target turnaround is within 48 business hours per address after scope confirmation.
projects.summary: Source-backed research distilled into concise briefs that separate verified facts, inference, conflicts, unknowns, and missing records.
projects.whatItProves: A software and data experiment can become a disciplined research workflow, real-property proof, and paid-service offer.
projects.hardPart: Jurisdiction records arrived with inconsistent structure, incomplete ownership signals, stale portal states, and chronology that had to be reconstructed rather than assumed.
projects.howItWasBuilt: AI assists with organizing and reviewing case material, implementation passes, and quality checks. It never approves evidence or acts as an autonomous permit reviewer; findings and delivery require human approval. Briefs preserve source limits and unknowns and do not make legal, title, architectural, engineering, entitlement, code-compliance, or government determinations.

engineeringNotes.summary: React and TypeScript shape the operational interface. Cloudflare Workers run the application edge, D1 holds structured case state, R2 keeps evidence private, and Better Auth protects the workspace. The packet engine produces consistent HTML and PDF deliverables from reviewed records.

projects.name: SGVTurf
projects.subtitle: An SGV homeowner planning and contractor-discovery system.
projects.currentStatus: The homeowner brief, 2026 turf-replacement rebate resource, city guides, and editorial system are live. Founding-contractor outreach is testing the referral side.
projects.summary: Connects local homeowner search intent to city guidance, official-source rebate context, a structured project brief, and relevant contractor discovery.
projects.oneLiner: A local-service site built around search intent, service-area pages and lead capture.
projects.stack: Local search · Official-source research · Lead capture
projects.whatItProves: Useful local information can form a clear acquisition path from search intent to a contractor-ready inquiry.
projects.hardPart: Rebate rules change, city context varies, and an empty contractor roster must not look like participation.
projects.howItWasBuilt: AI assists with research organization, city-page implementation, funnel iteration, and outreach preparation. Rebate claims are checked against official sources. The founding test is explicit about its limits: no contractor participation, lead volume, revenue, or result is claimed.

projects.name: Snapshot Studio
projects.category: Local business / AI search audit tool
projects.summary: A lightweight sales tool for turning local visibility problems into fast visual reports and improvement plans.
projects.oneLiner: Turns a business intake into a structured improvement snapshot and action plan.
projects.whatItProves: Small businesses can receive fast, visual snapshots of search visibility problems and practical improvement plans.
projects.hardPart: The offer started too broad, outreach responses were inconsistent, and report value had to be made obvious faster.
projects.howItWasBuilt: AI supports prospect research, report drafting, local search framing, landing-page passes, and a repeatable audit structure. The human work is closing the gap between a useful audit and a paid offer.

projects.name: Xibalba Pinball
projects.summary: A mythic five-ball score attack with touch controls, browser physics, and a global Wall of Champions.
projects.oneLiner: Browser pinball with physics, scoring and a global leaderboard.
projects.whatItProves: AI-assisted development can ship a weird, playable, visually distinctive browser game.
projects.hardPart: Table tuning fought the art direction, collisions misbehaved, and several visual passes missed the intended underworld mood.
projects.howItWasBuilt: Built with AI support for physics implementation, Phaser iteration, asset direction prompts, debugging loops, and mobile polish. Table feel, collision edge cases, and taste decisions were earned through failed passes.

projects.name: BounceBox
projects.subtitle: Physics Groovebox
projects.summary: A mobile-first physics groovebox that turns bouncing balls and AI-generated MIDI patterns into a playable instrument.
projects.oneLiner: A mobile music playground built with Web Audio, generative MIDI and dense touch controls.
projects.whatItProves: Browser-native physics, audio, generative controls, and mobile UI can become a distinctive playable instrument.
projects.hardPart: Rhythm feel, touch ergonomics, MIDI prompt boundaries, and dense performance controls all had to be tuned into something playable.
projects.howItWasBuilt: TypeScript iteration with a custom ChatGPT MIDI Lab for generative pattern design, plus mobile UI passes, control naming, and performance-state testing. The taste work was making unusual mechanics feel intentional.

projects.name: Danger Close
projects.summary: A tactical browser survival game about piloting a salvage drone through dead zones, collecting resources, surviving enemy pressure, and upgrading hardware between runs.
projects.oneLiner: Interactive browser experiment focused on fast tactical feedback.
projects.whatItProves: AI-assisted development can ship a polished browser game loop with sector selection, upgrade systems, enemy pressure, resource collection, survival pacing, and premium sci-fi interface design.
projects.hardPart: Early balancing passes created uneven pressure, dense combat states reduced clarity, and experimental systems did not always share a clean plan.
projects.howItWasBuilt: Used Codex and frontier AI models for gameplay systems, UI polish, enemy behavior, upgrade design, copy, testing checklists, and rapid iteration. Balancing is still evolving and visual density needs tuning.

projects.whatItProves: Research, editorial structure, local context, and frontend implementation can become a useful niche information system.
